Projects

What I've been building

Curriculum Design

"How Much Are the Apples?" — Unit 4 Lesson Pack

This is how I build a lesson from the ground up: start from one target structure — here, "How much is/are...?" — and design every piece of material to circle back to it, so students meet the same language in five or six different forms before the period ends. The teacher's plan sets clear objectives and a procedure timed to the minute (warm-up, presentation, guided practice, freer activity, wrap-up), so the lesson runs itself even for a substitute picking it up cold. From there I built out a full worksheet set: vocabulary matching, a grammar drill, a comic-strip reading text, a price-tag role-play, a "create your own shop" task, a board game that forces students to produce the target language to move around the board, and a cut-and-paste sorting activity for lower-level learners — plus printable price tags, play money and role cards so nothing needs extra prep on the day. This is one unit out of a full communicative-English curriculum I adapted for Thai secondary students, reviewed and approved for classroom use at Mathayom level.

Mathayom 1 100-minute lesson 7 worksheets + exit ticket School-approved curriculum
